title: Compute efficiency: binary keeps only 0% of the multipliers busy

body:
With NX8's 8-bit static formats, the tensor that loses most even in its best format is layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256: 32.1 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) in fp8_e2m5, measured on that tensor alone by the format search. Measured on 11 models with a format search (of 280 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 23.3 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst 12.8 dB (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae). 7 of 9 models with a prediction metric (top-1, perplexity or agreement) lose some of it; the most: microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (agreement 100% → 0%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's), PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (agreement 100% → 58%: the share of samples whose predicted class matches full precision's) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (token agreement 100% → 66%: the share of token positions whose predicted token matches full precision's).

The tensors that lose most in their best format (their own error): layernorm output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 32.1 dB), add output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.0 dB), mul output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 34.5 dB), layernorm bias in openai-community/gpt2 (fp8_e3m4, 34.5 dB), linear bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 34.7 dB), linear output in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, 35.5 dB), layernorm bias in BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.6 dB), linear output in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e3m4, 35.8 dB), add output in BAAI/bge-base-en (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB) and groupnorm bias in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (fp8_e2m5, 35.8 dB).

Separately, the error accumulated along the data path (every tensor before a node quantized too): div outputs end furthest from full precision, microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition keeping only -inf dB there. The outputs furthest from full precision in each model's best format set: div in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -inf dB), linear in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -3.0 dB), sub in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -2.4 dB), softmax in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -1.1 dB), relu in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -1.1 dB), mul in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (fp8_e2m5, -0.8 dB), div in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, -0.0 dB), softmax in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (fp8_e3m4, 0.4 dB), mul in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 0.5 dB) and aten in PekingU/rtdetr_r101vd_coco_o365 (fp8_e3m4, 0.9 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 3619 (45%), fp8_e3m4 3411 (43%), fp8_e1m6 940 (12%), ufp8_e2m6 39 (0.49%), ufp8_e3m5 1 (0.01%); 0.50% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where an output's own error in its format, times its data, is largest: silu in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e2m5, 42.4 dB), conv2d in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.4 dB) and upsample in stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5:vae (fp8_e1m6, 43.9 dB).

1 missing capability keep 28 operations in 3 models (of 8 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (28 operations in 3 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding) needs a workaround. It affects 28 operations in 3 models: 28 calls (0.91% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in openai-community/gpt2 and embedding in BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5. Cost today: 0 of 28 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 1 failed and 27 wait for one; 70 workarounds proposed, 9 passing its check, 13 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

title: Missing instructions: 28 operations in 3 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 510 of 899 tensors passed between kernels (57%) in 8 models: 341 for attention heads split or merged, 148 for other reshapes, 18 for pixels reordered and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 328 operations (328 calls, 11% of all calls; 101 G MACs, 4.21% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 118 and linear → add (other reshapes) 64; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (202), stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (128) and microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (51).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 510 of 899 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 875 operations in 8 models (875 calls, 29% of all calls), most often layernorm (217), silu (210) and groupnorm (113). Their quantized accuracy: worst -inf dB SQNR over 812 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 32.5, most 82 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 82 planned groups), over 8 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.4 powers of ten for bmm in jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (largest value 1.35e+05).

13 outputs in 1 model hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (12) and select_where (1), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

2 accuracy runs produced non-finite outputs (overflow or NaN).

0 kernels use over 80% of the 1,024-word instruction memory (IMEM) bank, of 1 kernel measured.
title: Resource limits: 875 operations limited by the LUT and up to 82 kernel launches per pass

body:
The IPU architecture's costs across the surveyed models, ranked from most to least significant:

1. **Resource limits** are the most widespread cost: 875 operations (29% of all calls) across 8 models are constrained by the 256-entry lookup table for activations like exp, GELU and reciprocal, with the worst accuracy at -inf dB SQNR, plus up to 82 kernel launches per pass and 2 runs producing non-finite outputs.

2. **Layout conversions** affect 510 of 899 tensors (57%) passed between kernels in 8 models — mostly for attention head splitting/merging — forcing the reading kernel to rearrange data, covering 328 operations (11% of calls, 4.21% of MACs), though cycle costs are not yet measured.

3. **NX8 format quantization** shows substantial accuracy loss: model outputs keep a median 22.2 dB SQNR against full precision (worst 12.8 dB), 7 of 9 models with a prediction metric lose some accuracy, and some tensors' accumulated errors are severe (e.g. div at -inf dB in one model).

4. **Missing instructions** (run-time addressing) block 28 operations in 3 models (0.91% of calls, no MACs) — all embeddings — from running directly on the chip; 27 still wait for a workaround, with no accuracy or cycle measurements yet.

5. **Compute efficiency** is the least quantified but potentially severe: binary formats keep only 0% of multipliers busy across 14 measured cases, meaning the pipeline cannot keep multipliers fed at all for that primitive.
